source.title: Stochastic learning flow: moment equations for stochastic gradient descent at finite step size

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied, including Results, Methods, Discussion, and Supplemental Information.
record.tranche_reason: The paper tests stochastic-learning-flow predictions and edge-of-stability dynamics, but does not measure training classification error or test the claim versions about interpolation, width, initialization, shortcuts, learning-rate recovery, or batch normalization.
record.gate_note: The network experiments report loss curves, parameter updates, covariance, and curvature thresholds. These do not report training classification error for a version in the claim. Results from cited prior work are not this study's own results.
record.test_reason: The study derives its own full-batch sharpness–covariance dynamics and a stationary sharpness of 2/η, directly bearing on V5's edge-of-stability component. V5 concerns loss and sharpness, so the record's requirement for training classification error incorrectly excludes it.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially accurate. More precisely, the authors conclude that SLF predicts tested ensemble dynamics at low and intermediate noise, deteriorates as non-Gaussian features emerge, analytically recovers a full-batch edge-of-stability stationary point, and predicts a lower mean-square stability threshold under minibatch curvature fluctuations.
record.recipe_differences: The paper develops and evaluates moment equations for stochastic gradient descent; it does not test the claim's training-error recipes.
record.method_sensitivity: Prediction quality changes with batch noise: it is successful at low and intermediate noise and breaks down as non-Gaussian effects become more pronounced. The reported edge-of-stability threshold is lowered by batch noise.

fits_no_version.finding: The nonlinear-network probe finds that minibatch curvature fluctuations lower the mean-square stability threshold; including the gradient–third-derivative correction changes predictions by less than 1%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: For minibatch SGD, curvature fluctuations can lower the local mean-square perturbation stability threshold below 2/η.

fits_no_version.finding: In a constructed one-dimensional loss, full-batch gradient descent at η=0.1 escapes a sharp local minimum and reaches a broader global minimum, whereas η=0.01 converges locally.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Finite learning rates can destabilize sharp local minima and permit escape in a constructed scalar loss landscape.

fits_no_version.finding: SLF predicts ensemble loss, parameter means and covariance at low and intermediate noise, with prediction quality deteriorating alongside non-Gaussian distributions.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Second-order moment equations can approximate finite-step SGD ensemble dynamics within a limited noise regime.

record.problems: The theory truncates moment equations at second order and loses predictive accuracy as parameter or loss distributions become non-Gaussian. The tested networks have at most a few thousand parameters; the authors say validity at larger sizes remains undetermined. The edge-of-stability analysis projects parameter dynamics along a single direction.
record.rows_left_out: No qualifying rows: reported outcomes concern loss prediction, parameter trajectories, covariance prediction, and curvature thresholds, none of which measure the training-error outcomes named in the versions.

untested.parts: All parts: CIFAR training classification error, label corruption, capacity, stopping and regularization.
All parts: spurious-minimum frequencies in two-layer ReLU networks and the effect of extra student neurons.
All parts: depth degradation, identity shortcuts and the specified alternative training recipes.
All parts: initialization comparisons, training speed and trainable depth.

Wide-network catapult recovery, transient loss increases, larger-rate divergence, and divergence from initially subthreshold curvature. The study also does not independently establish sustained empirical sharpness hovering while training loss falls; its full-batch result is a conditional analytical stationary point.
All parts: normalization comparisons, accuracy speed, learning-rate tolerance and Fixup.

missing.what: Record the analytical full-batch stationary-point result: covariance grows when λ1>2/η, feeds back to reduce sharpness, and admits λ1*=2/η with σ1²*=(2S1+ηQ1)/g1. Identify this as a conditional theoretical result, not an empirical training curve. The blanket exclusion in rows_left_out incorrectly treats it as irrelevant.

record.verdict_notes: There are no extracted rows to fix. Figure S1 measures one-step perturbation stability, not sustained training recovery or loss reduction. Its minibatch threshold shift does not challenge V5's explicitly full-batch threshold statement. The theoretical stationary-point result does not by itself establish convergence to that point or continued loss decline.

versions.untested_parts: Training classification error on CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100, random or corrupted labels, model size, stopping, and regularization.
Spurious minima frequency and student-versus-teacher width in two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems.
Depth comparisons of plain versus residual networks and training outcomes with special initializations or without normalization.
Activation-matched initialization, depth-dependent learning speed, orthogonal versus Gaussian initialization, and 10,000-layer plain convolutional training.
Recovery or divergence of training loss as learning rate crosses a stability threshold, and sharpness behavior during full-batch training.
Batch-normalization effects on accuracy speed or learning-rate tolerance, and Fixup residual-network performance without normalization.

relationships.condition: Analytical full-batch dynamics projected onto the sharpest direction, with progressive sharpening and a physically admissible stationary covariance.
relationships.reason: Section 2.5, equations (29)–(33), derives covariance growth above 2/η and covariance feedback opposing sharpening, yielding stationary sharpness 2/η. This supports the edge-of-stability mechanism conditionally; the evidence is in the text and absent from the record's rows.
relationships.display_finding: With an admissible stationary covariance, covariance growth above 2/η opposed sharpening and yielded stationary sharpness 2/η.
